If all products and services could be made using only 10% of available workforce, what are the best methods to reduce tensions between workers and non-workers and distribute wealth?

I think there are two approaches that would work: you can have everyone work an equal amount, taking turns and changing around every day or week, then pay each person according to how efficiently they worked (only volunteers would work, but people who don't volunteer and can work don't get paid), or you can have the most efficient workers work, having tests every now and again to see how efficient everyone is, and then pay the workers slightly more than everyone else so that people have an incentive to work efficiently.

Personally, I think the second method would work better. This is essentially the system we have now where unskilled workers get low-paying jobs like working in fast-food places and skilled workers become doctors or scientists. The system would be similar to this except instead of working in a low-paying job, unskilled workers would just not work at all. The payment to people who do work would have to be increased until it is at an equilibrium where there is the highest average quality of life overall. Another thing that would be important in this system is automation. The more robots that are built to automate jobs, the better, and this should be a very high priority.

For a frame of reference I'm a PhD level chemist but I design and build scientific equipment.

For the first system, the jobs that will most likey still be needed will be the high skill ones. Doctors, scientists, engineers, computer science, etc. In all of those types of fields the workers would be a lot less effective if they only work a a day or week here and there.

For the second system, if I'm working all the time because I'm very good at what I do I'm going to be pissed at only making slightly more. If I've spent years learning a high skill field and being good at it, the resentment won't take long to build. I'd rather use my skills to provide things on the black market or share them with people I like.

Which is why I said that we should increase payment until there is an equilibrium for the highest average quality of life. If some people don't work because they aren't being paid enough, so be it. If we are paying some people more than they should be paid, so be it. The point is to find a balance between these two where the most production is achieved for the inequality that results from it.
